title: Attosecond metrology of bright quantum light
authors: P. Stammer, J. Rivera-Dean, E. Pisanty, M. Lewenstein
abstract: Attosecond metrology is the ability to measure ultrafast optical light-wave oscillations, yet its approach has been limited to classical fields. Hence, the influence of the fluctuations of a quantum field on attosecond measurements has remained unexplored. Here, we close this gap by showing that the attosecond streaking measurement of bright quantum light is sensitive to quantum fluctuations of the optical field on the attosecond timescale. The distinct sub-cycle modulations allow to extract the properties of the squeezed field quadrature in regimes where conventional state tomography approaches reach their limitation. With the full quantum optical attosecond streaking scheme developed here, we provide a certification method that can measure quantum squeezing below the shot noise limit, thereby overcoming the problem of tomographically measuring bright quantum light. This opens the way towards quantum optical metrology of field fluctuations with attosecond temporal resolution.
summary: The paper introduces a method to measure quantum fluctuations in bright light by adapting attosecond streaking spectroscopy. By analyzing the Quantum Optical Streaking Trace, researchers can detect signatures of field squeezing that are invisible to classical measurement techniques. This opens a new avenue for performing quantum optical metrology with attosecond temporal precision.
main_problem: To extend attosecond metrology from classical field measurements to accurately quantify quantum fluctuations present in bright quantum light.
main_result: The developed Quantum Optical Streaking Trace (QOST) serves as a certification method capable of measuring quantum squeezing below the shot noise limit, overcoming limitations of conventional state tomography.
method: The authors utilize an attosecond streaking measurement scheme where photoionization by an XUV pulse followed by interaction with a quantized Infrared (IR) field allows for the calculation of the QOST via trace operations over the joint light-matter quantum state.
model_or_system: The system involves an electron interacting with an intense XUV burst and an arbitrary IR streaking field, which is modeled as a quantized electromagnetic field capable of being in squeezed vacuum states. The evolution is governed by unitary operators derived from the interaction Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Quantum Optical Streaking Trace (QOST), $	ext{SQ}(p, 	au)$, and its sensitivity to quadrature squeezing properties of the IR field.
important_parameters: Attosecond temporal resolution ($	au$), quantum squeezing parameters, and measurement regimes below the shot noise limit.
main_assumptions: The formalism is derived for an arbitrary light field (classical or quantum); approximations are made when comparing to quasi-classical limits, though the full quantum treatment is emphasized.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the QOST for bright squeezed vacuum fields, showing distinct sub-cycle modulations revealing field fluctuations and allowing quadrature squeezing measurement; comparisons are drawn between amplitude vs. phase squeezed states.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the gap in current metrology (classical limitation), develops the quantum formalism using the QOST, derives mathematical expressions comparing full quantum traces to semi-classical limits, and finally demonstrates how specific field fluctuations manifest as measurable modulations in the trace.
why_interesting: This work directly bridges advanced concepts in quantum optics (squeezing, non-Gaussian states) with ultrafast time resolution techniques (attosecond metrology), providing a novel diagnostic tool for fundamental quantum physics research.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Streaking of a bright squeezed vacuum field. Schematic illustration of the quantum optical attosecond streaking, where the IR streaking field consists of quantum light such as a bright squeezed vacuum and is delayed by τ with respect to the coherent XUV pulse. The distinct subcycle modulations in the streaking trace reveal the field fluctuations and allow for measurement of quadrature squeezing.

FIG. 3. Attosecond streaking trace of bright quantum light. Quantum optical streaking trace for a displaced squeezed state D(α) |ξ⟩with amplitude squeezing in (a) and phase squeezing in (b). The squeezing intensity of Isq = 5 × 10−5 a.u. is the same for all cases. For the amplitude and phase squeezed state we considered the ratio of Icoh/Isq ∼6, for the intensity from the coherent and the squeezed contribution.

FIG. 2. Attosecond streaking a bright squeezed vacuum field. Quantum optical streaking trace of a BSV field show- ing distinct sub-cycle 2ω oscillations around a vanishing mean value of the streaking field with prominent quantum fluctu- ations. Here, we set the squeezing intensity of the streaking field (ω = 0.057 a.u.) to Isqu = 5 × 10−5 a.u., using helium (Ip = 0.904 a.u.) for the atomic system, and used a coherent XUV pulse of Ω= 3.3 a.u. and IR pulse duration (FWHM) of 5 fs.

FIG. 4. Physical origin of the variance distribution for anti- squeezed light. Streaking trace at fixed time-delay τ for the classical fields resembling the amplitude and phase-squeezed vector potential. For (a) and (b) the field Aam(t), while for (c) and (d) the field Aph(t) was considered.
